questions.stem:
Case study: Mr Adeyemi, the administrative officer of a secondary school in Oyo, complains that staff files are often missing. Clerks keep files on top of cabinets, borrowed files are not recorded, and letters about the same teacher are kept in different places. A new clerk, Fatima, is asked to reorganise the filing system. She plans to use numbered files for all staff with an index, to introduce out guides and to move old records to storage.
(a) Identify three problems in the existing filing practice. [6 marks]
(b) Explain how each of Fatima's three proposals would solve the problems. [9 marks]
(c) State four qualities of a good filing system. [4 marks]
(d) State three advantages of electronic filing that the school could consider. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: files are left on top of cabinets, so they are lost or damaged
2 marks: borrowed files are not recorded, so their location is unknown
2 marks: related letters are scattered across different files
3 marks: numbered files with an alphabetical index give each teacher one file that can be located quickly
3 marks: out guides record who borrowed a file and when, so it can be traced
3 marks: moving inactive records to storage frees space and reduces congestion in current files
1 mark: simplicity
1 mark: accessibility / quick retrieval
1 mark: security / confidentiality
1 mark: economy / flexibility / compactness
1 mark: saves storage space
1 mark: faster search and retrieval
1 mark: easy back-up and sharing / reduced loss of documents
questions.explanation: Problems: files left on cabinets, no record of borrowed files, scattered correspondence. A numerical system with an index gives one traceable file per teacher; out guides track borrowings; transferring dead files decongests the system. A good system is simple, accessible, secure, economical and flexible. Electronic filing saves space, speeds search and allows back-up and sharing.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the document used at each of the following stages of a business transaction: (i) a buyer asks for prices; (ii) the seller replies with prices; (iii) the buyer orders goods; (iv) the seller sends goods; (v) the seller bills the buyer; (vi) the seller reduces the amount owed for returned goods. [12 marks]
(b) State two uses of a statement of account. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: letter of enquiry
2 marks: quotation / price list / catalogue
2 marks: order / local purchase order
2 marks: delivery note / waybill / advice note
2 marks: invoice
2 marks: credit note
2 marks: shows the balance owed at the end of the period
2 marks: reminds the buyer to pay / allows the buyer to check his records
questions.explanation: The sequence is enquiry, quotation, order, delivery note (or waybill), invoice and, for returns, a credit note. A statement of account summarises transactions, shows the balance due, reminds the customer to pay and lets him reconcile his records.

questions.stem:
(a) State four duties of a storekeeper. [8 marks]
(b) A store received 400 units of an item at N120 each and later 600 units at N130 each. Calculate the value of the 1,000 units and the weighted average cost per unit. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: receiving and checking goods against delivery notes and orders
2 marks: storing goods safely in the right place
2 marks: issuing goods on proper requisition
2 marks: keeping stock records such as bin cards / reordering at the right level / stocktaking
2 marks: 400 x 120 = 48,000
2 marks: 600 x 130 = 78,000
2 marks: total value N126,000
2 marks: average cost = 126,000 / 1,000 = N126
questions.explanation: Storekeepers receive and check goods, store them safely, issue them on requisition, keep records, reorder and take stock. Value = 48,000 + 78,000 = 126,000; weighted average = N126 per unit.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following forms of communication with one example each: (i) verbal; (ii) non-verbal; (iii) visual. [6 marks]
(b) Explain four barriers to effective communication in an office. [8 marks]
(c) What is feedback? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: verbal: use of words, oral or written, e.g. telephone call or letter
2 marks: non-verbal: gestures, facial expressions, posture, e.g. nodding
2 marks: visual: charts, graphs, pictures, e.g. a sales chart
2 marks: physical barrier, e.g. noise, distance, faulty equipment
2 marks: psychological barrier, e.g. emotions, prejudice, poor listening
2 marks: socio-cultural barrier, e.g. language, beliefs
2 marks: organisational barrier, e.g. long chain of command, poor structure
2 marks: the response of the receiver showing whether the message was understood
questions.explanation: Verbal communication uses words (calls, letters); non-verbal uses gestures and expressions; visual uses charts and pictures. Barriers are physical, psychological, socio-cultural and organisational. Feedback is the receiver's response confirming understanding.

questions.topic: Health, Safety and Welfare in the Office
questions.stem:
(a) State four health hazards in an office. [4 marks]
(b) Explain four ways of preventing accidents in an office. [8 marks]
(c) State two welfare services an employer may provide for office staff. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: slippery or wet floors
1 mark: trailing cables and overloaded sockets
1 mark: poor lighting and ventilation
1 mark: poor posture / eye strain from screens / fire hazards
2 marks: keep floors dry and corridors free of obstructions
2 marks: maintain electrical equipment and avoid overloaded sockets
2 marks: provide and train staff on fire extinguishers and exits
2 marks: proper storage of materials / first-aid box / safety signs
2 marks: canteen / transport services
2 marks: medical care / recreational facilities / staff housing
questions.explanation: Hazards include wet floors, trailing cables, poor lighting, poor posture and fire. Prevent accidents by keeping floors dry and clear, maintaining electrical equipment, providing fire equipment and training, safe storage and first aid. Welfare services include canteens, transport, medical care, recreation and housing.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the stages a job applicant goes through from seeing an advertisement to being employed. [10 marks]
(b) State three items that should appear in a curriculum vitae. [3 marks]
(c) State three rules for a successful interview. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: reading the advertisement and studying the job requirements
2 marks: writing a letter of application
2 marks: attaching a curriculum vitae and credentials
2 marks: attending tests/interview after being shortlisted
2 marks: receiving a letter of appointment, accepting and undergoing medical/induction
1 mark: personal details
1 mark: educational qualifications
1 mark: work experience / skills / referees
1 mark: arrive early and dress neatly
1 mark: answer questions clearly and honestly
1 mark: show good manners / bring required documents / prepare beforehand
questions.explanation: The applicant reads the advertisement, writes an application, encloses a CV and credentials, is shortlisted for tests and interview, then receives an appointment letter, accepts and undergoes medical checks and induction. A CV contains personal details, education, experience, skills and referees. At an interview, be punctual, neat, honest, clear and polite.
